ov: Small, fast antelopes, mostly fawn-coloured, living in herds in the deserts, grasslands and savannas of Africa and in south-west and central Asia and India.
rg: Africa, south-west and central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.
df: Fine, easily digested plants and leaves.

cf.tip: Gazelles are one group of antelopes.

fx: Some gazelles can sprint at 100 km/h or hold 50 km/h.
Thomson’s gazelles stot, running and leaping high, when a predator threatens them.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact is half confirmed: Thomson’s gazelles stot (jump high) when threatened, but the article doesn’t say why.
